issues.legal_issue: Prolonged living together as husband and wife gives rise to a rebuttable presumption of a valid marriage, and the evidence relied on did not rebut that presumption.
material_facts: The couple had lived together as husband and wife for many years, and it was undisputed that the child was born to them.
The woman and her child were not mentioned in the father’s will or in the family partition compromise.
The witnesses’ depositions did not state that the couple had not lived together.
The first appellate court found a valid marriage by applying the presumption, but the High Court reversed that finding in a second appeal.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in treating the presumption as rebutted on these circumstances. The Supreme Court restored the first appellate court’s finding.
issues.legal_principle: Under Gokal Chand v. Parvin Kumari, prolonged cohabitation as husband and wife raises a rebuttable presumption of a valid marriage. On the facts here, omission from the father’s will and family compromise did not rebut the presumption, and the witness testimony did not contradict the cohabitation. The High Court was therefore not justified in interfering with the first appellate court’s factual finding.

rule.if: appeal_from_second_appellate_reversal and prolonged_cohabitation_as_spouses and child_born_of_relationship and (omitted_from_family_documents or witnesses_did_not_deny_cohabitation)

predicates.appeal_from_second_appellate_reversal: A party appealed after a second appellate court reversed a first appellate court’s finding in a civil property dispute.
predicates.prolonged_cohabitation_as_spouses: A man and a woman lived together for a prolonged period as husband and wife.
predicates.child_born_of_relationship: A child was born to the man and woman who lived together.
predicates.omitted_from_family_documents: The woman and her child were not mentioned in family documents relied on to challenge the relationship.
predicates.witnesses_did_not_deny_cohabitation: The witnesses’ evidence did not deny that the couple had lived together.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal challenges a second appellate reversal, prolonged cohabitation as spouses raises a marriage presumption that remains unrebutted where the cited omissions or testimony do not contradict the cohabitation, so the first appellate finding is restored.

issues.legal_issue: A person who receives an exclusive share through partition may settle that share because it no longer retains its ancestral or coparcenary character.
material_facts: A partition compromise gave the transferor an exclusive right over his share.
The transferor executed a settlement of that share in favour of his wife and children.
A beneficiary under the settlement later conveyed an interest to the appellant, whose title was challenged in the property suit.
issues.conclusion: The share became the transferor’s exclusive property upon partition, so the settlement was valid and the beneficiary could convey the interest derived under it.
issues.legal_principle: When a partition gives a person an exclusive share, the ancestral or coparcenary character of that property comes to an end and the person becomes its exclusive owner. The owner may execute a settlement in favour of a spouse and children, and a beneficiary may convey the interest obtained under that settlement. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this ruling.

rule.if: property_title_suit and partition_gave_holder_exclusive_share and exclusive_owner_settled_share_for_family and beneficiary_transferred_interest_under_settlement

predicates.property_title_suit: The dispute is a civil suit concerning title to property.
predicates.partition_gave_holder_exclusive_share: A partition gave a person an exclusive right to a particular share of property.
predicates.exclusive_owner_settled_share_for_family: The person holding the exclusive share executed a settlement in favour of family members.
predicates.beneficiary_transferred_interest_under_s: A beneficiary later conveyed an interest obtained under the settlement.

issues.definition: In a property-title dispute, an exclusive share obtained through partition may be settled by its owner for family members, and a beneficiary may convey the interest received under that settlement.
